To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the beta-1 adrenoceptors blockade in rats with talinol causes a sodium-uretic response accompanied by an increase of blood flow and no PO2 changes.

the blockade of beta-1 adrenoceptors in the rat kidney is associated with a sodium-uretic response accompanied by a decrease in the sodium reabsorption, an increase of blood flow to the cortical and outer layers of the kidney with no changes in the oxygen tension.

blockade of beta-1 adrenergic receptors with talinol in anesthetize rats caused sodium-uretic response accompanied by a decrease of sodium reabsortion in the kidney and increase of renal blood flow in the cortical and medullary layers with no changes of oxygen tension in the renal medulla.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new mechanism of the sodium- diuretic effect of the beta-1 adrenergic blocking agents.
the possibility to use the beta-1-adrenoreceptor blocker talinolol as a diuretic in the therapy of hypertension.
the mechanism of sodium diuresis induced by a blockade of beta 1-adrenoceptors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the beta-1 adrenoceptor blocking agents, talinolol in particular, are able to exert a sodium-uretic response in rats, which is accompanied by an inhibition of sodium re-absorption and by an increase in the blood flow in the renal cortical and medullary areas.
beta-adrenoreceptors of the beta-1 type in the rat kidneys are not involved into the regulation of the blood flow, oxygen tension or sodium transport.
talinolol is a specific beta 1-adrenoceptor blocking drug.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the beta 1-blockade in the kidney entails an increase in the blood flow and an inhibition of sodium reapsorption.
beta-adrenoreceptor blockade in kidneys is followed by inhibition of sodium transport, an increase of the renal blood flow and a decrease of the PO2.
beta 1 adrenoreceptor blockade with talinol causes a hemodynamic shift in favor of the cortex, and an inhibition of sodium re-absorption.
The main takeaway from our work is that
talinolol is a powerful inhibitor of the beta-adrenoceptors of the kidneys, and its action is independent of the beta-2 adrenoreceptors.

blockade of beta 1-adrenoceptors in the kidneys of rats is accompanied by a decrease of sodium reabsorbtion in the renal tubules, which is due to the increase of blood supply to the renal cortical and external layers.

the beta 1 adrenoreceptor blockade with talinol is accompanied by inhibition of the channel transport of Na and an increase of blood flow.
